topic: How does a car differential let the wheels turn at different speeds?

claims.claim: When cornering, the outer wheel travels farther than the inner wheel.
claims.passage: Purpose: outer wheels must travel farther than the inner wheels (larger radius)

claims.claim: A differential lets the wheels on one axle rotate at different speeds.
claims.passage: lead: allows the wheels at each end of a drive axle to rotate at different speeds while cornering

claims.claim: A pinion from the engine side drives a ring gear, which turns the carrier.
claims.passage: Ring-and-pinion design: ring gear driven by a pinion connected to the transmission; caption: ring gear rotates the carrier

claims.claim: Small planet gears in the carrier connect the two axle (output) gears.
claims.passage: parts list: output gears, planetary gears, carrier

claims.claim: On a curve one wheel turns faster and the other slower while the planet gears turn on their shafts.
claims.passage: Purpose figure captions: right wheel turning faster when turning left; planet gear rotation follows kinematically from the average property
claims.note: planet-gear rotation is a kinematic consequence of c6, not a quoted sentence

claims.claim: The carrier's speed is the average of the two wheel speeds.
claims.passage: lead: rotational speed of one shaft is the average of the speeds of the others

guardrails: open differential, simplified; not to scale
terms: planet gears / axle gears (source wording: planetary / output gears)
open_questions: Source is an encyclopedia (secondary); an engineering text would strengthen c5/c6 for publication
